## Summary

This security context reveals nuclei's historical risk surface dominated by sandbox escapes (7), auth bypasses (4), path traversals (4), and code execution (3+2 unsigned) across JavaScript/tengo scripting, template loading/verification, and file-access sinks. Recurring themes: incomplete enforcement of sandbox/local-file-access flags (-lfa), signature verification gaps on direct vs. workflow/DAST load paths, and SSRF/network-policy bypasses via DSL helpers and LDAP dialing. A large cluster centers on the JavaScript sandbox (require, eval, file I/O, krbforge/mysql/ldap libs) and on template verification cache/guard hoisting. The most important posture is ensuring every loader and every JS/tengo module enforces the same opt-in gates and path/network policies with no sibling-path asymmetry.

## Top Risks

### 1. Sandbox Escape: `pkg/js/compiler/pool.go, v2/pkg/protocols/javascript/js.go, v2/internal/runner/processor.go, v2/pkg/protocols/headless/engine/engine.go` (high)

Multiple independent escapes in JS/tengo scripting engines: require() bypassing local-file rules, eval and file reads unrestricted, broad stdlib imports, and headless no-sandbox misuse. Recurring pattern of sandbox flags not enforced on all execution paths.

Evidence: 6f2ade6a9b427c284c15a43445f9c7f055e60e5d, c35162c8ef061a96dd74b54c8f022c1a41cf5833, cf2a98b03d76327c20fb0183b7f1c849eb692c91, 96049a32fa70aef0483d4180d386a57b3c2d973a, df55f7a2eb591a7949b5c66a9c54db54aa28f450

### 2. Auth Bypass: `pkg/templates/signer/tmpl_signer.go, pkg/templates/compile.go, pkg/catalog/loader/loader.go, pkg/protocols/http/request.go` (high)

Template signature verification bypasses via metadata cache reuse, signature extraction flaws, and unverified template loading. Also cookie-jar auth bypass. Verification must be cryptographic and enforced on every load path.

Evidence: 0da993afe6d41b4b1b814e8fad23a2acba13c60a, 4534e9cb3034ebe5cc7b0cecabe399b6fb9ce0e4, 9bd4db3f74aedd067af568df4f9198a8a090f68b, a976ca8d3f6a18c9ca746c8ce73f28fdcd518642

### 3. Code Execution / Unsigned Template: `pkg/catalog/loader/loader.go, pkg/templates/workflows.go, pkg/templates/templates.go` (critical)

Unsigned templates can execute arbitrary code when signature guards are hoisted or missing on direct vs. workflow/DAST load paths; cache poisoning also allows unsigned execution. Requires guard on every loader.

Evidence: 9de96e4dda5a03da963b9ae6582f03ea55791a76, 1c440e755a97471c56fb0276ee8a8c4132974645, fac0b7196d2fbca56c8af8ff8e1899c111041a37, e86f38299765b82ad724fdb701557e0eaff3884d, fa56800fcca3c8c8fe8e8dec28584210ca1527de

### 4. Path Traversal: `pkg/installer/versioncheck.go, pkg/catalog/config/nucleiconfig.go, v2/pkg/protocols/common/generators/load.go, v2/internal/runner/update.go` (high)

Zip-slip, ignore-file write, custom-template trust boundaries, and payload file loads all use path prefix checks that can be bypassed via canonicalization; sandbox flag often not enforced.

Evidence: e908de14fa92fcee346253cab2452240605873c5, 20cbf0bd73893c1270582c9778b6b26a5cb11206, e7fb40a41308f6c41267e858d1781eb67f7e0572, f9c214a66f37a00fc29fe64232b690e6285ec59c

### 5. SSRF / Network Policy Bypass: `pkg/operators/common/dsl, pkg/js/libs/ldap/ldap.go, v2/internal/runner/proxy.go` (high)

DSL helpers and LDAP dialing bypass scan-level network restrictions (-lna/-eh); DNS escapes and wrong-host validation enable SSRF. Proxy settings can be hijacked or mis-validated.

Evidence: c50f92fdd3fb78d563300d2cda9c79bea1a427ce, 9def9af7e3f7ebcf5cd561c37b623b9999ee7572, a167e6c57b80f5dc7be231231b62d7c594ee2770, 0e46d3e0410f89e4af41099f5cd38fa7f54ae54f

### 6. External File Write/Read: `pkg/js/libs/krbforge, pkg/js/libs/mysql, pkg/js/libs/smb` (high)

JS libraries (Kerberos ticket forging, SMB, MySQL) write or read arbitrary files unless the -lfa policy is enforced on each sink; also custom output paths.

Evidence: 3a8b65cb45f121fcdf418f60e5177ed9f250c122, c5611b9ac4c553c220129eb100e7bfbd32e5adb8, 9611926a9a1ca99e8ed554d1b26fbeff60e06368

## Shared Attack Surfaces

Capabilities guarded by more than one past fix on different code paths. A guard enforced on one entry point is often missing on a sibling; verify each alternate path before assuming it's covered.

### 1. Template loading/compilation/execution with signature verification

- Guard that should hold everywhere: template.Verified, template.TemplateVerifier, signer.Verify, parsed.Verified, DisableUnsignedTemplates, LoadTemplatesWithTags guard on all branches
- Entry points: `pkg/catalog/loader/loader.go`, `pkg/templates/templates.go`, `pkg/templates/workflows.go (workflowExecutor)`, `pkg/templates/compile.go`, `pkg/templates/signer/tmpl_signer.go`
- Check: Inspect the workflow executor and DAST branch in loader.go: they may enforce -dut/verify on direct loads but skip on sub-loaders; require all guards (verification + unsigned-disable) on every path including workflows that load code templates.
- Evidence: 9de96e4dda5a03da963b9ae6582f03ea55791a76, 1c440e755a97471c56fb0276ee8a8c4132974645, fac0b7196d2fbca56c8af8ff8e1899c111041a37, e86f38299765b82ad724fdb701557e0eaff3884d, fa56800fcca3c8c8fe8e8dec28584210ca1527de, 4534e9cb3034ebe5cc7b0cecabe399b6fb9ce0e4

### 2. JavaScript module execution sandbox (local file access and network policy)

- Guard that should hold everywhere: allowLocalFileAccess flag (-lfa), local-file path validation, require registry rebuilt per-execution, network policy IsHostAllowed, file:// scheme blocking, safe module allowlist, eval disabled
- Entry points: `pkg/js/compiler/pool.go`, `v2/pkg/protocols/javascript/js.go`, `pkg/js/libs/krbforge/krbforge.go`, `pkg/js/libs/mysql/mysql_private.go`, `pkg/js/libs/smb/smb.go`, `v2/internal/runner/processor.go (tengo)`, `v2/pkg/protocols/common/protocolstate/headless.go`
- Check: Hunt for JS module or tengo workflows that call a restricted API without re-checking -lfa or host allowlist; verify each library (krbforge, mysql, smb) applies path canonicalization and that require() disallows absolute paths outside template dir.
- Evidence: 6f2ade6a9b427c284c15a43445f9c7f055e60e5d, c35162c8ef061a96dd74b54c8f022c1a41cf5833, 3a8b65cb45f121fcdf418f60e5177ed9f250c122, 9611926a9a1ca99e8ed554d1b26fbeff60e06368, c5611b9ac4c553c220129eb100e7bfbd32e5adb8, cf2a98b03d76327c20fb0183b7f1c849eb692c91, d3928e080d819f25306bfbaecc399f03516db5aa

### 3. Network dialing with host allowlist and scan restrictions

- Guard that should hold everywhere: -lna/-eh network restrictions, IsHostAllowed (on resolved controller host, not just domain), proxy validation (ProxyInternal flag, connectivity check), hop-by-hop header stripping
- Entry points: `pkg/operators/common/dsl (resolve, public_ip, jarm, dns Query)`, `pkg/js/libs/ldap/ldap.go (newLdapSession, Dial)`, `v2/internal/runner/proxy.go (loadProxyServers)`, `internal/server/proxy/proxy.go`, `pkg/protocols/http/request.go`
- Check: Check DNS helper paths and LDAP controller resolution: they must validate the actual dialed IP/host against -lna/-eh, not just the input domain; verify proxy enablement is gated by ProxyInternal and dialed host is re-checked.
- Evidence: c50f92fdd3fb78d563300d2cda9c79bea1a427ce, a167e6c57b80f5dc7be231231b62d7c594ee2770, 9def9af7e3f7ebcf5cd561c37b623b9999ee7572, 0e46d3e0410f89e4af41099f5cd38fa7f54ae54f, 3f5c055aca1499642caf4f40e8cf55ad32bd4da9, 6dfd955715a09e958ddd24b828f74d06930c7838

### 4. Local file read/write policy enforcement (path traversal and arbitrary file access)

- Guard that should hold everywhere: path canonicalization + containment check, -lfa flag gating, sandbox mode path prefix check, file:// scheme blocking, os.WriteFile content validation
- Entry points: `pkg/installer/versioncheck.go`, `pkg/catalog/config/nucleiconfig.go`, `v2/pkg/protocols/common/generators/load.go`, `v2/internal/runner/update.go`, `pkg/js/libs/mysql/mysql_private.go`, `pkg/js/libs/krbforge/krbforge.go`, `v2/pkg/protocols/common/protocolstate/headless.go`
- Check: Identify any template workflow that loads payload files, ignores, or updates templates via an alternate API (e.g., sub-loader) and verify it performs canonical path checks plus -lfa gating; the zip-slip and payload-load paths are most at risk.
- Evidence: 20cbf0bd73893c1270582c9778b6b26a5cb11206, f9c214a66f37a00fc29fe64232b690e6285ec59c, e7fb40a41308f6c41267e858d1781eb67f7e0572, e908de14fa92fcee346253cab2452240605873c5, 3a8b65cb45f121fcdf418f60e5177ed9f250c122, 9611926a9a1ca99e8ed554d1b26fbeff60e06368, d3928e080d819f25306bfbaecc399f03516db5aa

## Fixed-Issue Fingerprints

These are real security fixes mined from git history. Use them as regression checks.

- **Code Execution / Arbitrary File Write** (high) [CWE-434]: This commit fixes arbitrary file write in the Kerberos ticket forging library by enforcing the file policy and restricting output destinations, mitigating path traversal and unauthorized file creation.
  - sink: `krbticket generation writing to a custom output path and SMB session handling`
  - fix: Validate destination against existing file policy and restrict output to template directory; reject custom paths
  - commit: https://github.com/projectdiscovery/nuclei/commit/c5611b9ac4c553c220129eb100e7bfbd32e5adb8 (2026-09-26)
- **SSRF / Network Policy Bypass** (high) [CWE-918]: This commit fixes a security vulnerability by enforcing scan-level network restrictions (-lna/-eh) on DSL helper functions that previously could perform unrestricted network I/O, preventing SSRF and network policy bypass.
  - sink: `helper execution performing network I/O without respecting scan -lna/-eh restrictions`
  - fix: Propagate scan options to enforce -lna/-eh on network operations; reject restricted IPs, DNS escapes, trailing dots
  - commit: https://github.com/projectdiscovery/nuclei/commit/c50f92fdd3fb78d563300d2cda9c79bea1a427ce (2026-09-23)
- **Logic Flaw** (medium) [CWE-20]: Prevents accidental high/critical findings based solely on non-deterministic LLM output by requiring confirmation or explicit override.
  - sink: `Template validation allowing LLM matcher as sole matcher on high/critical severity templates`
  - fix: Reject templates with LLM as sole matcher unless allow-sole field set
  - commit: https://github.com/projectdiscovery/nuclei/commit/fe14cf5d2ccac4d15b61666facd9daaa4370ed7c (2026-09-11)
- **Proxy Security Bypass** (high) [CWE-436]: Hardens the intercepting proxy to prevent unwanted proxy chaining, credential leakage, and replay of sensitive headers.
  - sink: `unmodified http.Transport honoring ambient HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY env vars and replaying hop-by-hop headers (Connection, Proxy-Authorization) to target`
  - fix: explicit forward proxy configuration and stripping of hop-by-hop headers
  - commit: https://github.com/projectdiscovery/nuclei/commit/6dfd955715a09e958ddd24b828f74d06930c7838 (2026-09-10)
- **Security Configuration Bypass** (medium) [CWE-287]: Per-execution filter options could silently clear the engine's baseline ExcludeTags deny-list, allowing dangerous templates to run; the fix restores those exclusions.
  - sink: `restoreBaseExcludeTags`
  - fix: preserve baseline exclusions after per-execution filters
  - commit: https://github.com/projectdiscovery/nuclei/commit/09c1bbf51b58a6e0638649e31bb1a419e3c73be1 (2026-09-03)
- **Auth Bypass** (high) [CWE-287]: Honors disable-cookie by preventing the shared cookie jar from being applied when cookie handling is disabled, closing a path where cookies could be reused across requests.
  - sink: `SetCookieJar(input.CookieJar)`
  - fix: Adds !request.DisableCookie check before applying shared cookie jar

- **Path Traversal** (high) [CWE-22]: The installer now validates the downloaded nuclei-ignore file content before writing it, preventing malicious or unexpected content from being written to the ignore file path.
